headline: Fuel prices remain unchanged for November, second month in a row
summary: Bangladesh's Energy and Mineral Resources Division has announced that fuel prices will not be revised in November. This marks the second consecutive month without a price change after September's increase.
details: Fuel prices for diesel, octane, petrol, and kerosene will remain at their current retail rates nationwide throughout November. This decision follows a confirmation order from the Energy and Mineral Resources Division.
Diesel will continue to be sold at Tk 135 per litre, octane at Tk 165, petrol at Tk 160, and kerosene at Tk 155. These prices were initially set on September 20 and took effect from November 1.
The Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation had previously requested the unchanged rates in a letter dated October 26. This comes after a Tk 20 per litre increase for all four fuels in September.

Prior to the September hike, diesel was priced at Tk 115 per litre, octane at Tk 145, petrol at Tk 140, and kerosene at Tk 135. The September increase brought diesel prices up by Tk 35 per litre since April.

The government typically adjusts fuel prices monthly based on an automatic pricing mechanism that reflects international market trends. However, regular adjustments have not been made in recent months.

Consumers will continue to pay the September prices, despite the automatic pricing mechanism's intended role in aligning domestic fuel costs with global oil prices, which had risen due to conflict in West Asia.

headline: 5-hour delay: PM's flight leaves Japan after technical glitch
summary: A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying the Prime Minister was delayed at Narita International Airport due to a spoiler alert in the cockpit.
details: The Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying the Prime Minister departed from Japan's Narita International Airport after a delay of over four and a half hours.
The aircraft was originally scheduled to depart Tokyo at 6:18 PM local time on Thursday, October 29, and was expected to arrive at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport by 10:30 PM.
The delay occurred after boarding was completed and the plane had begun its pushback. A spoiler error signal appeared in the cockpit, prompting the flight to be suspended immediately.
Technical teams worked to resolve the issue, with initial estimates suggesting the repair would take between two to four hours.
After the technical glitch was fixed, the flight finally took off for Dhaka.
caption:
A technical glitch in the cockpit caused a 5-hour delay for the Prime Minister's flight from Tokyo to Dhaka.

The Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying the Prime Minister departed from Japan's Narita International Airport after a delay of over four and a half hours.

The aircraft was originally scheduled to depart Tokyo at 6:18 PM local time on Thursday, October 29, and was expected to arrive at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport by 10:30 PM.

The delay occurred after boarding was completed and the plane had begun its pushback. A spoiler error signal appeared in the cockpit, prompting the flight to be suspended immediately.

Technical teams worked to resolve the issue, with initial estimates suggesting the repair would take between two to four hours.

After the technical glitch was fixed, the flight finally took off for Dhaka.

Source: Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com
